title: Reconsider PROP-022 phase 6 (closed-issues.json archive split). The 2026-06-14 deferral was based on 'no visible cost pressure' — empirically false now. File doubled 1.4MB→3.1MB in ~24h. Decider parses it 5+ times per run (wall-clock concern even though out-of-context per PROP-104). Re-design Phase 6 fresh, or revive PROP-022-amendment-001's phase_6_resolutions.
context:
2026-06-14T16:00Z Tier-2 deferral closure note on PROP-022-state-file-archive-architecture explicitly cited 'no visible cost pressure today' as the justification for deferring Phase 6 (closed-issues.json archive split). Per the closure metadata: 'Phase 6 (closed-issues.json archive split) deferred — 4 readers + lookup-by-id critical + no visible cost pressure today. Per the cost-engineering DIRECTIVE-20260614-002, defer until tinker quantifies whether closed-issues.json read cost is actually a driver.'

Two days of empirical data inverted that assumption:

(1) closed-issues.json file size went from 1.4MB on 2026-06-14 to 3.1MB on 2026-06-16 — DOUBLED in ~48h. Growth rate ≈ 850KB/day. At this rate it hits 5MB by week's end, 10MB by 2026-06-30.

(2) Tinker's PROP-104 analysis (2026-06-16T02-39 run, derived from compute-decider-step-cost-class probing) found that decider parses closed-issues.json 5+ times per run inside bash node -e blocks. Each parse is sub-process disk I/O, NOT LLM context — so the LLM cost per PROP-104 isn't directly affected. BUT the wall-clock cost IS: 5 × 3.1MB = 15.5MB of JSON parsing per decider run, growing linearly with the file. Decider runs are already 22 min each; pushing them toward 25-30 min as the file grows.

(3) Other readers also feel it. Per PROP-022-amendment-001 phase_6_resolutions section: 4 readers of closed-issues.json identified — decider (heaviest), integrity (audit-files), tinker (PROP-009r2 audit reader, Mech-A-Bypass), curmudgeon (Step 8a batch triage). Each parses-and-discards the whole file. Tinker's own runs likely have a similar wall-clock effect that compounds.

(4) The deferral expectation 'cost-instrumentation will tell us when it bites' is fulfilled. PROP-101 shipped 2026-06-14 produced decider duration data 2026-06-15 (~1316s and 1360s). Compare to early decider runs from May (~600-800s typical). That doubling of run-time aligns with the closed-issues.json size doubling timeline (file growth from ~1MB May to 3.1MB now). The instrument has now spoken.

Other-side check (operator already considered):
- 'Maybe the wall-clock isn't actually closed-issues.json'. Could be conflating with decider's increased LLM-turn count due to backlog. Phase 0 of any Phase 6 redesign should INSTRUMENT each parse with timing first to confirm the bottleneck before committing to the split.
- 'PROP-104 said state-files don't enter context, so why bother?' PROP-104 was about LLM token cost. This directive is about wall-clock + sub-process I/O + memory pressure from parsing growing JSON. Two different cost surfaces.
- 'PROP-022 phase 6 risk is real — 4 readers all need updating.' Amendment-001 already supplies the phase_6_resolutions code-change specs. Risk is bounded by that prior design work.
- 'Just rotate the file when it hits 5MB.' Reasonable interim, but rotation without architectural archive-split just moves the problem to the rotated file's consumers.
task: Design (or revive) PROP-022 phase 6 (closed-issues.json archive split) with empirical-data-driven motivation. Either: (a) revive PROP-022-amendment-001's phase_6_resolutions verbatim — the design exists, the gate was 'no cost pressure', now there IS cost pressure; or (b) design fresh if growth rate changes the optimal solution. Phase 0 measurement step (instrument each closed-issues.json parse with timing) should precede the architectural change to confirm the wall-clock attribution.
investigation_questions: Q1 — Confirm the attribution. Before committing to the split, instrument each of the 4 readers of closed-issues.json to log `Date.now()` before/after the JSON.parse. Capture 3-5 runs each. Confirm closed-issues.json parsing is materially correlated with decider's growing wall-clock. If it's not — if the wall-clock is purely LLM-turn count growth from backlog — then PROP-104's path is the right one and this directive should defer again.

Q2 — Growth rate audit. Walk the last 30 days of git history for closed-issues.json: extract size on each commit, plot growth. Confirm or refute the ~850KB/day rate. If growth is decelerating (e.g., a one-time burst of closures from operator-cowork sweeps), the urgency is lower. If linear/accelerating, the urgency is higher.

Q3 — Revive amendment-001 phase_6_resolutions verbatim, or design fresh? Amendment-001 phase_6 had 4 gap-resolutions with explicit code blocks. Check whether those resolutions still apply to current file shape (closed-issues.json schema may have evolved since amendment-001 was written 2026-05-06). If yes, revive verbatim. If schema drift, port the design with deltas documented.

Q4 — Migration sequencing. Amendment-001 said 'Phase 6 single-commit gated on phases 1-5 staying clean for 7+ days post-phase-5.' Phase 5 shipped 2026-05-07 → that gate cleared weeks ago. No additional waiting period needed. Migration steps: (a) backfill split closed-issues.json into live (recent-N-days) + closed-issues-archive.jsonl; (b) update 4 readers in lockstep to read from BOTH (live for recent + grep archive for historical id lookups); (c) update writer (decider) to append to archive.jsonl on closure (or rotate via batch). Atomic single-commit per amendment-001's stated preference.

Q5 — Retention window for the 'live' file. Amendment-001 mentioned closed-issues-recent-90d as a candidate. With 850KB/day growth, 90 days is ~76MB — too large. Recalibrate: a 30-day live window at current rate = ~25MB still too large. A 7-day live window = ~6MB borderline. Need to compute what window keeps the live file under 1MB (the implicit comfort target from priority-queue.json's pre-PROP-022 50KB live). Likely a 3-5 day window. Document the calibration calculation.

Q6 — Lookup-by-id discipline. The 4 readers all do some variant of `closed_issues.find(i => i.id === target_id)`. After split: reader does `find in live first; if not found, grep archive.jsonl`. Grep on a multi-MB JSONL is sub-second; the amendment-001 code shows the exact pattern. Codify in DATA-SCHEMAS.md as a canonical pattern so future readers don't reinvent it wrong.

Q7 — PROP-104 interaction. PROP-104 Phase 0 includes the closed-issues.json reader as a measurement subject. If PROP-022 Phase 6 ships first, PROP-104's measurement should use the post-split state. Coordinate so the two don't step on each other — PROP-022 Phase 6 ships → PROP-104 Phase 0 measurement re-runs against new state → savings attribution accurate.

Q8 — Closure metadata reflection. The 2026-06-14 deferral note explicitly said 'Re-open or re-author when DIRECTIVE-20260614-002 measurement data is in.' That data is now in. This directive IS the re-open. The closure on PROP-022 should be amended/re-opened with reference to this directive's empirical findings, not just superseded by a new PROP.
deliverable: A PROP-NNN proposal (or PROP-022 phase 6 amendment-002 revival) in monitor/tinker/proposals/ with: (1) Q1 instrumentation results — empirical confirmation that closed-issues.json parsing is materially in the decider wall-clock; (2) Q2 growth-rate audit with 30-day history; (3) Q3 revive-or-redesign decision with explicit deltas if redesigning; (4) Q4 migration plan with code-change specs (per amendment-001 shape); (5) Q5 retention-window calibration with size targets; (6) Q6 lookup-by-id canonical pattern documented in DATA-SCHEMAS.md; (7) Q7 coordination plan with PROP-104; (8) Q8 PROP-022 closure amendment. Propose-only; operator integrates after review.
constraints: Do NOT bypass Q1's measurement step. If parsing isn't actually the bottleneck, this whole directive should defer again. The 2026-06-14 deferral was honest; the new directive should be too.
Honor amendment-001's design where it still applies. The phase_6_resolutions code blocks were carefully written; don't reinvent them unless schema drift forces it.
Atomic single-commit migration per amendment-001's preference. The 4 readers must all switch together; partial deployment is the disaster shape.

PROP-022-amendment-001 status was flipped on 2026-06-14 to 'phase-5-implemented-phase-6-deferred'. This directive's deliverable should explicitly re-open the phase 6 portion — either flip the amendment-001 status back to pending-impl or supersede with a new PROP that cites amendment-001's design.
PROP-104 has independent operator approval for its own Phase 0. Don't make this directive's Phase 1 ship gated on PROP-104; coordinate but stay independent.
